niche: Mind Hacks, AI Secrets, Bizarre Body Science & Hidden Power Dynamics

ideas.title: The Interactive Red Furniture Mind Hack
ideas.angle: The video uses a high-speed priming sequence of numbers and shapes to force the viewer to think of 'Red Chair'. It challenges the viewer to comment if it worked, creating a viral feedback loop.

hook.en: I bet I can read your mind right now.

ideas.reason: Interactive 'mind reading' tests are currently the highest-performing sub-genre in dark psychology, consistently hitting 100%+ APV because viewers re-watch to see how they were manipulated.
sources: The Science of Psychological Priming - Nature

ideas.title: The 3-Second Shoulder Touch Power Move
ideas.angle: Shows a specific micro-behavior (The 'Upper Arm Squeeze') that instantly establishes dominance and rapport in a conversation. It triggers a comment debate on whether it's 'creepy' or 'powerful'.

hook.en: Touch their shoulder like this to win any argument.

ideas.reason: Power dynamics and 'status hacks' are trending on TikTok and YouTube Shorts, particularly those involving physical micro-interactions which are highly visual and easy to demonstrate.
sources: The Definitive Book of Body Language by Allan and Barbara Pease
Journal of Nonverbal Behavior - Tactile Communication

ideas.title: The Impossible Nose Itch Brain Glitch
ideas.angle: A live challenge where viewers stare at a specific point on the screen while the narrator describes an 'itch' on their nose. It exploits the 'Mirror Neuron' reflex to make their face actually itch.

hook.en: You are about to feel a ghost on your face.

ideas.reason: Sensory 'glitches' achieve high VVSA because they provide an immediate physical sensation, forcing the viewer to engage and comment 'It actually worked!' or 'I felt nothing'.
sources: Mirror Neurons and Sympathetic Itching - British Journal of Dermatology
Psychology Today: The Science of Itching
